question: to the President of the European Council Erik Kaliňák (NI), Judita Laššáková (NI) Subject:

In the wake of the recent Hungarian parliamentary elections and related political developments, calls to revisit the Beneš Decrees have re-emerged in public discourse (including in the European Parliament). Yet the Beneš Decrees, just like the Bierut Decrees in Poland or the AVNOJ Decrees in the former Yugoslavia, were fundamental pillars of the post-war order in Europe, constituting purely historical legislation and that currently has no practical effect. 1.

Does the President of the European Council agree that these three sets of decrees constitute an enduring historical part of the post-war European order, upon which today’s European Union itself is founded?

Does the President of the European Council not consider that the stability and cohesion of the Union would be seriously undermined if a discussion were to begin at the highest political level regarding the revision of these historical acts, which could undermine legal certainty, historical continuity and mutual trust among Member States?
